summary: New Hampshire has no state law tying smoke or carbon monoxide alarms to the sale of a home: the state alarm rules depend on the type of building and when it was built, not on a closing.
alarmType: RSA 153:10-a requires automatic fire warning devices meeting NFPA 101 and NFPA 72 in multi-unit dwellings and rental units. A single-family dwelling is covered only if it was built or substantially rehabilitated after January 1, 2010. The statute names the NFPA standards rather than a power source, so it does not specify sealed 10-year battery, hardwired or interconnected alarms. The state fire marshal may adopt enforcement rules but may not require a sprinkler system in a one- or two-family dwelling that otherwise complies.
coAlarms: Carbon monoxide detectors meeting NFPA 720 are required in the same buildings — multi-unit dwellings, rental units, and single-family homes built or substantially rehabilitated after January 1, 2010. Not required where the dwelling has no attached garage and no fuel-burning appliance; if either is added later, a CO detector becomes required. Nothing in the statute ties this to a sale.
